title: Router Message Reachability
statement:
A network has `n` wireless routers. Each router has a unique name and a fixed position `(x, y)` on a 2D plane, and every router has the same wireless range `R`: two routers can communicate directly when the Euclidean distance between them is **at most** `R`.

When a router receives a message it forwards it to every router within its range, and those routers forward it in turn, so a message can travel across several hops. For example, with range 10, a router at `(0, 0)` reaches a router at `(0, 8)`, which can pass the message on to a router at `(0, 17)`, while a router at `(11, 0)` is out of range of all three and never receives it.

Router `source` sends a message. Decide whether router `target` eventually receives it. A router always counts as reaching itself.
inputFormat:
The first line contains two integers `n` and `R`.
Each of the next `n` lines contains a router name (a string with no spaces) and two integers `x` and `y`.
The last line contains two names: `source` and `target`, both of which appear in the list.
outputFormat: Print `YES` if `target` can receive the message sent by `source`, otherwise print `NO`.
constraints: Names are unique and consist of 1 to 10 letters or digits

examples.explanation: A and B are 8 apart, which is within the range of 10, so A reaches B directly.
A is 17 away from C, too far for a direct hop, but A reaches B (distance 8) and B reaches C (distance 9), so B relays the message to C.
D is at distance 11 from A, about 13.6 from B and about 20.2 from C. No router that can receive the message is within range of D.

def gen(rng):
    import string
    def fmt(R, pts, s, t):
        lines = [f"{len(pts)} {R}"] + [f"{nm} {x} {y}" for nm, x, y in pts]
        lines.append(f"{s} {t}")
        return "\n".join(lines)
    def names(n, maxlen=6):
        seen, out = set(), []
        while len(out) < n:
            L = rng.randint(1, maxlen)
            nm = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits) for _ in range(L))
            if nm not in seen:
                seen.add(nm)
                out.append(nm)
        return out
    base = [("A", 0, 0), ("B", 0, 8), ("C", 0, 17), ("D", 11, 0)]
    tests = [fmt(10, base, "A", "B"), fmt(10, base, "A", "C"), fmt(10, base, "A", "D"), fmt(10, base, "D", "C")]
    tests.append(fmt(5, [("x", 3, 3)], "x", "x"))
    tests.append(fmt(5, [("a", 0, 0), ("b", 3, 4)], "a", "b"))
    tests.append(fmt(5, [("a", 0, 0), ("b", 3, 5)], "a", "b"))
    tests.append(fmt(1, [("a", -1, 0), ("b", 0, 0), ("c", 1, 0)], "a", "c"))
    tests.append(fmt(1000000, [("p", -1000000, -1000000), ("q", 1000000, 1000000)], "p", "q"))
    tests.append(fmt(1000000, [("p", -1000000, -1000000), ("q", 0, 0), ("r", 1000000, 1000000)], "r", "p"))
    for _ in range(40):
        n = rng.randint(2, 9)
        R = rng.randint(1, 6)
        nm = names(n, 3)
        pts = [(nm[i], rng.randint(-10, 10), rng.randint(-10, 10)) for i in range(n)]
        s, t = rng.choice(nm), rng.choice(nm)
        tests.append(fmt(R, pts, s, t))
    # long chains with spacing exactly R (inclusive range), shuffled
    n = 1000
    nm = names(n, 8)
    xs = [i * 1000 - 500000 for i in range(n)]
    pts = [(nm[i], xs[i], 0) for i in range(n)]
    order = list(range(n))
    rng.shuffle(order)
    tests.append(fmt(1000, [pts[i] for i in order], nm[0], nm[n - 1]))
    tests.append(fmt(1000, [pts[i] for i in order], nm[n - 1], nm[0]))
    # same chain with one gap that is one unit too wide
    pts2 = [(nm[i], xs[i] + (1 if i >= 500 else 0), 0) for i in range(n)]
    tests.append(fmt(1000, [pts2[i] for i in order], nm[0], nm[n - 1]))
    # a zig-zag chain on a diagonal
    pts3 = [(nm[i], -500000 + i * 600, (i % 2) * 800) for i in range(n)]
    tests.append(fmt(1000, [pts3[i] for i in order], nm[0], nm[n - 1]))
    # random dense cloud
    pts4 = [(nm[i], rng.randint(-10000, 10000), rng.randint(-10000, 10000)) for i in range(n)]
    tests.append(fmt(1000, pts4, nm[3], nm[500]))
    tests.append(fmt(300, pts4, nm[7], nm[900]))
    return tests
